title: Machine learning predicts 12-month amputation risk in arterial disease with diabetes
summary: Across 1,919 patients with lower extremity arterial disease and diabetes from four Chinese hospitals (amputation rate 14.0%), a gradient boosting model, the best of ten algorithms, reached internal AUC 0.860 and external AUC 0.828 (n = 538). Rutherford grade, Barthel Index, wound status and CRP were among the predictors, with a complementary Fine-Gray model for competing risk. The study is retrospective with no prospective test, and the external cohort comes from the same national setting.
ai_technology: Ten machine-learning algorithms (best gradient boosting) with LASSO, random forest and Boruta predictor screening

evidence.tested: Internal validation (n = 414) and external validation (n = 538) at separate hospitals, retrospectively.
evidence.unknown: Prospective performance and clinical benefit; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning models predicted 12-month amputation from clinical predictors.
